original_hook: $LSK is up over 83% in 24 hours, but the real technical footprint isn't the headline move—it's the systematic shift in its pullback floors. Rather than a single low-liquidity wick that unwinds immediately, LSK has built four progressively higher support floors on the 1H chart: $0.4590 ➔ $0.5144 ➔ $0.6131 ➔ $0.6970. This stair-step structure indicates persistent spot absorption, where buyers step in higher during low-volume consolidations to absorb sell pressure. The invalidation level is precise: an hourly close below $0.6970 breaks the rising floor ladder and confirms profit-taking off the $0.8476 wick. Structural continuation requires a firm 1H close above $0.8000 on strong volume. 📊 LSK 1H: price $0.7929 • support $0.3412 • resistance $0.8476 • TP1 $0.9742 • target $1.1008 • SL / invalidation $0.3412 (long bias). Levels are chart-derived scenarios, not guarantees. What confirmation on $LSK would make you treat this setup as real rather than an early headline move?
